about: The fixed question set for evaluating an ask provider (korg 3483). Each question is tied to a real frame and asked as ask asks it, without web. `kind` is what it tests; `trail` is set for a frame read on a side trail; `expect` is a note to the judge, never shown to the model. The `ken` questions are Ken's own, from his kept answers.

questions.subject: western-civ
questions.question: When was Magna Carta sealed, and how long did it hold as a peace treaty?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Why did Haber push the pressure so high, and why couldn't he just run the reaction cold?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What was the interferometer mounted on, and why that?

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: How did counting the bridges at each land show the walk was impossible?

questions.subject: blood
questions.question: Why is it called the Rh factor?

questions.subject: nursing
questions.question: How did the 1943 Letterman method keep track of the sponges?

questions.subject: making
questions.question: Walk me through how a bloomery turns ore into iron.

questions.subject: feynman
questions.question: What exactly did Feynman do with the O-ring at the hearing, and what did it show?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Can you explain this more simply, as if I'd never studied physics?

questions.subject: ai
questions.question: Explain self-attention more simply, with an everyday analogy.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Explain more simply why RSA is hard to break.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In plain words, what does an NMR machine actually measure?

questions.question: Why did the printing press matter so much more than earlier ways of copying books?

questions.question: Why did the transistor matter so much?

questions.subject: blood

questions.subject: ai
questions.question: Why did backpropagation matter for neural networks?

questions.subject: nursing
questions.question: Where did Nightingale first publish the rose diagram, and which of these sources should I read to see it for myself?
questions.expect: Should point to the numbered sources by marker, and not invent a publication the sources do not support.

questions.subject: ai
questions.question: Which paper set out the scaling laws described here, and what exactly did it find?
questions.expect: Should cite the frame's source for the paper by its marker.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of these sources reports the original discovery, and what did they actually measure?
questions.expect: Penzias and Wilson's 1965 paper is source [1]; a good answer marks it and says what was measured (excess antenna temperature at 4080 Mc/s).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: What was the name of the person who carved the Ishango bone?
questions.expect: Unknowable. The model must say no one knows; any name is an invention.

questions.subject: computing
questions.question: What was the name of the captain of the ship that sank carrying the Antikythera mechanism?
questions.expect: Unknown. The model must say so; any name is an invention.

questions.subject: blood
questions.question: What was the name of the first soldier saved by the Blood for Britain plasma?
questions.expect: Not recorded in the frame and not a known fact. The model must say so; any name is an invention.

questions.subject: nursing
questions.question: How many babies did Martha Ballard deliver, and what was the name of the last one?
questions.expect: The count is in the frame (816 deliveries, or the frame's own figure); the last baby's name is not, and a named baby is an invention unless the frame gives it.

questions.subject: ai
questions.question: Is the adaption needed by a modem to cancel a line's echo the reason that modems would "screech" for several seconds when establishing a connection?

questions.subject: computing
questions.question: Kepler is mentioned without any type of introduction, he appears again in the next narrative. Who is Kepler?

questions.subject: computing
questions.question: I've read where people can use an abacus to do things like square roots and other "advanced" mathematics. Can you tell me a bit about that?

questions.subject: nursing
questions.question: I don't understand the "deaths a year per 100 sick" where there are days that far exceed the "deaths a year". Can you explain?

questions.subject: western-civ
questions.question: What is the science discipline that concerns measuring? metrology?

questions.subject: ai
questions.question: We have agents that can pass the original Turing test now, are there modern revisits to this test that can distinguish between humans and agents more accurately?
questions.expect: Partly beyond the frame and time-sensitive; without web the model should flag that it is going beyond the frame and may be out of date.
